extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs) and Incident Management Team (IMT) members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and performance expectations for Public Information Officers and Incident Management Team members handling incident information, media relations, staffing, logistics, safety coordination, and transitions during all-hazards incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-scene PIO role (taking the local temperature)
rubrics_metrics.description: On-scene Public Information Officers are the key to 'taking the local temperature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be present on-scene to assess local sentiment and the immediate environment; that local assessment should inform messaging and media engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-stage rapid assessment and response
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first stages of an incident, Public Information Officers must quickly assess the current situation and respond to immediate public and news media demands for incident information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act rapidly to supply basic, accurate information; triage media/public demands and prioritize the most urgent informational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze incident potential and plan information actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the incident’s potential, project public and news media demands for incident information, and plan a course of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forecast how the situation may evolve and anticipate future information needs, staffing, and messaging; use that forecast to create an information plan for the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible scale of PIO operations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the incident occurs on a PIO’s home unit they might be the only PIO; if small, the information function may be handled from the office with one or two co-workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to operate alone or in a small team; scale your response to the incident size and available personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum equipment/communications needs for information office
rubrics_metrics.description: A Public Information Officer does not need an elaborate setup—only a couple of telephones for incoming and outgoing calls, an easel chart, maps, basic office supplies, a radio or scanner, connectivity to the internet, and a television and/or radio to monitor news reports and incident messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure basic but reliable communications and monitoring tools are available to respond and coordinate information rapidly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go-Kit readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a pre-assembled Go-Kit stocked with supplies needed to get started; include a bag of personal items if asked to deploy out of area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enough critical information/materials to operate for the first 72 hours without support; understand transportation/weight limits and keep kit updated with current Federal/State laws and safety guidelines. Refer to sample Go-Kit contents list (Handout 2-3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and reliable information sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency dispatcher and agency radios/scanners are not usually the best places to get quality information; for larger incidents, use ICS Form 209 Incident Status Summary as the official upward reporting form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying solely on scanners or dispatcher chatter—these can be risky and misinterpreted. Use official forms (e.g., ICS Form 209) and Situation Unit outputs for authoritative status. Be aware media may listen to scanners and may overreact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rumor awareness and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and be aware of rumors, but do not believe them. Rumors tell you what the public might be thinking and/or what is being talked about in the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor rumors to gauge public perception, but verify via reliable sources before including in official messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess personnel skills/experience and delegate accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize experience levels of personnel and delegate tasks accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign tasks that match personnel experience; avoid assigning critical tasks to inexperienced staff without supervision or support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment considerations for selecting PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider agency community relations, previous incident and public affairs experiences, normal duties at home base, writing and speaking skills, day/night effectiveness, transportation, communications capabilities, and uniform status when selecting/assigning PIOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match individual strengths (e.g., on-camera comfort, radio skills) to task requirements; if someone is not comfortable or experienced on-camera, use radio or other outlets instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for special needs and political/protocol considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider special needs such as political protocol (e.g., Political Protocol Officer during election year) and realistic expectations about what resources will be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order resources as needed but be realistic about availability; anticipate political/special requirements that could affect messaging and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and credentials for deployed personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure personnel have required training records (Is everyone’s PTB signed?), get credit for training, and meet position training standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain training documentation, require necessary position training for new assignees, keep trainee positions full, and proactively recommend advanced training for high performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Command & General Staff members
rubrics_metrics.description: IC expects all C&G staff to attend meetings/briefings on time and prepared; resolve disputes before planning meeting; share Essential Elements of Information (EEI) thoroughly; maintain the incident action planning process and a positive professional demeanor; promote NIMS/ICS; take decisive action when performance standards are not met; support tactical operations; take care of self and team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must be punctual, prepared, supportive of the IAP process, model professional behavior, and monitor team fatigue/stress. Emphasize information sharing and unit cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Safety Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety Officer should be fully engaged in the IAP process, identify/manage/mitigate hazards, keep IC informed on accident/illness trends, promote 100% safety compliance, and provide a relevant safety message in each IAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety must be integrated into planning and communications; require timely, actionable safety inputs for each operational period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Public Information Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep incident personnel up-to-date on major current affairs; coordinate with Liaison Officer on stakeholder relations; identify and inform IC about emerging political/public issues; represent the IC in off-site PIO activities; promote positive impressions of information and interviews; ensure IC is prepared in appearance and mentally for camera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO is the IC’s information representative—ensure accuracy, timeliness, political awareness, and that the IC is media-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Liaison Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Address cooperating agency/stakeholder concerns positively; identify and coordinate with involved agencies/NGOs; provide a positive impression of the incident to other agencies; lead Agency Representatives; coordinate with the PIO; keep IMT aware of issues with cooperators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison must proactively track and coordinate stakeholder relations and ensure their concerns are integrated into incident actions and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Logistics Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage ordering to meet incident needs; anticipate supplies ahead of need; coordinate with supporting EOC; work closely with Operations to ensure logistical support; ensure IC has best facilities/equipment; act in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistics should be proactive, anticipate needs, and maintain cordial coordination with supporting entities to prevent operational gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Finance Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise and counsel staff on fiscal/contract/administrative matters; be prepared to provide cost analysis; attend briefings; coordinate with staff and cooperating agencies; possess knowledge to operate the Finance Section effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide fiscal inputs and cost information promptly to support operational decisions and IC requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Operations Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend strategies to reach objectives; keep IC and C&G informed on planned tactics; order resources within constraints; report unusual events and provide daily updates; insist safety procedures be followed; maintain effective communication with cooperating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations must communicate tactics, resource needs, and safety considerations clearly and timely to inform the IAP and IC decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander expectations of Planning Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide effective leadership and organization of meetings/briefings; ensure the organization follows the IAP process on time and accurately; maintain a thorough overview of incident activities to provide complete information for planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning must coordinate inputs, meet deadlines for IAP, and ensure situational awareness across the IMT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer expectations of Incident Commander
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety Officer expects the IC to emphasize safety in communications/actions and to support tactic changes for safety reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC must back safety recommendations and integrate them into tactical planning and public messaging where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer expectations of Public Information Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive to any accidents or other safety problems on the incident and coordinate what is released to the public, both media and locals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO should work with Safety to ensure casualty/accident information is accurate, appropriate for release, and not compromising investigations or victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer expectations of Liaison Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific information regarding problems with assisting/cooperating agencies and identify potential safety problems related to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison must highlight interagency safety readiness and coordination issues to the Safety Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer expectations of Logistics Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply personnel/equipment needs and coordinate with the Medical Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistics should ensure resources to meet safety/medical needs are procured and available quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer expectations of Finance Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Process accident reports timely, maintain exchange of safety-related information (excessive work hours, contract violations), and coordinate accident/injury information from Compensation/Claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finance must support timely documentation and reporting related to injuries and safety issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer expectations of Operations Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain close working relationship in tactics development, understand possible hazards, be flexible to change tactics that cannot be mitigated, provide information on unusual hazards, and avoid surprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations must integrate Safety feedback into tactics proactively and notify Safety of unusual field hazards immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer expectations of Planning Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Safety Officer in strategy/tactics meetings, provide briefings on situation and critical areas, include Safety in briefings, provide updates/feedback on safety responses, and provide info on personnel/resources availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning must ensure safety inputs and status are part of the IAP and operational briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Officer expectations of Incident Commander
rubrics_metrics.description: IC should approve press releases in a timely manner; cooperate with media requests; cooperate with public information meetings; provide direction on media expectations and social media messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC must enable PIO to act by providing timely approvals and clear guidance on messaging boundaries and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Officer expectations of Safety Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety Officer should summarize safety issues and provide daily reports of any accidents/injuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO relies on Safety to supply accurate safety information for public messaging and press briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Officer expectations of Liaison Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify key agencies, their roles, and any issues; provide communications materials to cooperating/assisting agencies as appropriate; help with communication strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison should ensure external partners receive coordinated communications and are included in outreach when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Officer expectations of Logistics Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Communication Plan; provide transportation; provide facilities and communication equipment for information office at ICP and other locales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistics supports the PIO by ensuring physical and technical infrastructure for information operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Officer expectations of Finance Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide current incident costs and provide press-worthy items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finance should furnish cost data that may be relevant to media queries and timely, cleared items suitable for public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Officer expectations of Operations Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on resources, special activities, and incident status; be open to allowing media access; provide press-worthy items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations must coordinate with PIO on what operational information is releasable and facilitate media access consistent with safety/security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Officer expectations of Planning Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide times of press briefings; coordinate on ICS Form 209; review information in press releases for accuracy; summarize development of incident; provide information on resource status; help with communication strategy; provide press-worthy items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning should supply situational summaries and status updates to enable accurate press briefings and release content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer expectations of Incident Commander
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise and counsel on issues presented by assisting/cooperating agencies; provide overall mission and direction; show willingness to engage with stakeholders when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC should provide clear mission direction so Liaison can effectively manage external agency relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer expectations of Safety Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide advice on hazards and issues particularly affecting cooperating and assisting agencies and input on 'safety readiness' of those agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety inputs should include interagency implications so Liaison can manage partner expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer expectations of Public Information Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention cooperating and assisting agencies/organizations in press releases; distribute information material to them; provide coordination/notification of public meetings and press conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate acknowledgements and communications so partner agencies are informed and included per agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer expectations of Logistics Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide transportation, facilities, and communication equipment; provide status of ordered resources; provide medical status of any personnel injured/ill from cooperating and assisting agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistics must ensure cooperating agency personnel needs and reporting are supported and communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer expectations of Finance Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Report excessive hours; report injuries/accidents to non-agency personnel; provide information on agency-specific pay-offs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finance should track and report administrative items affecting cooperating agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer expectations of Operations Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure safety and welfare of all personnel; share information and rationale on use of other agency personnel; establish availability of special resources from cooperators for Operations utilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations must coordinate use of cooperating-agency personnel and resources transparently to Liaison and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer expectations of Planning Section Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the IAP accurately reflects all cooperating/assisting agencies and organizations and coordinate status of those resources (e.g., demobilization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning must include partner agency resources and demobilization plans in the IAP to avoid omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team written operating procedures and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop written operating procedures and team-specific guidelines so members know what is expected; ICs should write basic operating guidelines and secure buy-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document roles, meeting schedules, acceptable timeframes, communications procedures, dispatch expectations, and responsibilities to reduce confusion during stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: How IC expects the team to work (meeting/process standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: IC should define meeting schedules, acceptable timeframes (e.g., planning meetings no more than 30 minutes and participants ready), communications while responding, which team members retrieve information, and other operation expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and enforce predictable processes (start times, responsibilities) to create a professional operating tempo and minimize delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-specific expectations and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State position-specific expectations (including the IC’s own role) and direct which personnel must provide written summaries for the team’s Narrative Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear written position statements help personnel meet expectations and ensure necessary documentation is produced for after-action records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance rating process for team members
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandate a rating process for all team members and personnel assigned to an incident; use specific responsibilities delineated in team guidelines as individual rating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use performance ratings to identify readiness for advancement and areas needing improvement; require ratings for all activations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-incident intra-team communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster routine information sharing prior to deployment (e.g., email updates) and maintain a team phone list with cell, pager and fax to smooth communications during incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-incident communication builds cohesion and reduces friction during response. IC should facilitate this flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing personnel development and cross-training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide hands-on development, keep trainee positions full, assure position training, recommend advanced training for high performers, and cross-train members in multiple functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage mentoring, trainee assignments, and stepping-back by leaders to develop subordinates; value cross-functional knowledge to increase team versatility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-incident critiques and improvement processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct post-incident critiques for team members only to identify successes, areas for improvement, required materials for next activation, and additional training requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make critiques a standard team process to build toward improved responses and update team procedures accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism standards for IMT members
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for highest professional management: know jobs/roles/required interactions, ensure identification of team members (hats/name tags/vests), punctuality, approachability and listening to field personnel, availability of IAPs to all who need them, timely interaction with responsible jurisdiction, orderly and complete paperwork, and use of visual presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional behavior includes clear ID, punctual meetings, accessible plans, thorough documentation (time records, narrative report), and use of visuals to convey information quickly (IAPs, schedules, safety messages, maps, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitioning an incident to an IMT (systematic handover)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitioning is a process to familiarize a team to a situation in progress and set agency strategic priorities; it should transfer the most information possible and require documentation for later reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an Agency Administrator Briefing or similar transition form, document the transfer, review the form yearly to incorporate new needed items, and approach transitions systematically to avoid dropping critical information.
